title: Consolidate routing rulebook and introduce typed contract verifier
creator: Maya Patel
description: Replace the ad-hoc routing rule interpreters with a single consolidated 'rulebook' and a typed contract verifier. The goal is to make region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variant resolution deterministic, easier to reason about, and statically checkable before runtime. This ticket covers schema design, static contract checks, runtime guardrails, a migration adaptor for existing policies, and an initial rollout for hosted customers. The verifier must catch: invalid region expressions, ambiguous tier precedence, incompatible fallback variant types, and deprecated clause usage.
acceptance_criteria: New rulebook schema (v1) documented in Confluence and approved by PM and Security
Typed contract verifier implemented and runs as a pre-deploy CI check for policy changes
Runtime guard added to the policy engine to reject policies that fail verification with clear error messages
Migration adaptor translates at least 95% of existing customer policies into v1 rulebook without manual edits
Performance regression <= 5% P95 request latency on routing evaluation path in staging
Unit + property tests cover region algebra, tier precedence lattice, and fallback resolution permutations
implementation_notes: Introduce a compact typed IR for routing rules: selectors (region, tier, model-capabilities), predicates, and outcome variants
Verifier runs in two phases: static type/shape checks and compatibility checks against active model catalog
Keep runtime evaluation fast by compiling verified rulebook to a small decision tree cached per-tenant
Support an opt-in strict mode for early adopters to enforce no-implicit-fallthrough semantics
Add detailed telemety tags during evaluation to surface why a route was chosen (or why policy was rejected)
migration_plan: Scan customer policies and classify into easy/maybe/manual buckets (scripted analysis job)
Auto-translate easy bucket and surface diffs in admin console for review
Provide a compatibility shim that accepts old DSL for 3 months with logging recommending v1 mappings
Run shadow verification for all incoming policy changes for 6 weeks before hard-blocking
Coordinate with Solutions & Customer Success for enterprise customers on a case-by-case migration plan
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Complex legacy policies may not be translatable. Mitigation: fallthrough shim and manual review process
Risk: Verifier false-positives blocking legitimate policies. Mitigation: provide bypass with audit trail and rapid hotfix path
Risk: Runtime performance hit due to richer checks. Mitigation: compile-to-tree cache + microbenchmarks in CI
Risk: Customers confused by new error messages. Mitigation: include actionable migration hints and links to docs in errors
testing: Create a fuzz test harness that generates region/tier combinations and asserts deterministic routing output
Property tests for precedence: assert transitivity and determinism across ordering changes
Integration tests that run verifier as a GitHub Action and block PRs that introduce schema violations
Load test routing evaluation path with synthetic traffic to assert P50/P95 latency targets
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable verifier for internal policies only and run migration scripts (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (beta): opt-in for self-serve tenants via console toggle, collect feedback (4 weeks)
Stage 3 (enforce): after 6 weeks of stable beta and migrations, enable hard-blocking mode for new policy changes
Emergency rollback: compatibility shim toggle to re-enable legacy interpreter if a severe outage is detected
